title: Nebula: Distributed Position-Independent Caching for LLM Serving
summary: Nebula replaces prefix-caching-centric distributed KV reuse with a cluster serving framework that treats position-independent cache segments as first-class objects, adding remote PIC reuse, parallel prefill, and cluster-wide cache management. Its cost is substantial serving-system complexity: optimistic accounting plus event-driven state tracking, adaptive PC/PIC capacity splitting via ghost-hit feedback, and a unified prefill completion-time model for parallelism and placement. It can fail when the assumed multi-segment reuse pattern is weak, when optimistic cluster accounting becomes inaccurate under fast-changing cache state, or when KV transfer and scheduling overheads outweigh prefill savings on a single-GPU deployment.
rationale: The paper targets cluster-wide distributed serving and cache coordination, which exceeds the reader's single 24 GB GPU/API-constrained production environment, so it is relevant to track but not adopt now.
technique: Distributed position-independent KV cache for LLM serving

claims.statement: Nebula replaces prefix-caching-centric distributed KV reuse with a cluster serving framework that treats position-independent cache segments as first-class objects, adding remote PIC reuse, parallel prefill, and cluster-wide cache management. Its cost is substantial serving-system complexity: optimistic accounting plus event-driven state tracking, adaptive PC/PIC capacity splitting via ghost-hit feedback, and a unified prefill completion-time model for parallelism and placement. It can fail when the assumed multi-segment reuse pattern is weak, when optimistic cluster accounting becomes inaccurate under fast-changing cache state, or when KV transfer and scheduling overheads outweigh prefill savings on a single-GPU deployment.

Nebula reduces median TTFT by an average of 61.4% versus the strongest existing baseline across four models and four RAG/agentic workloads (factor 1/(1-0.614)=2.59), and recovers an average of 76.1% of the tokens missed by prefix caching.
